title: All-New iPad mini is Here with OLED Display
summary: Apple updated the iPad mini with an 8.5-inch OLED display, an A20 Pro chip, IP67 water resistance, and a 5.4mm body. Explore our full breakdown of specs, new features, performance, and retail pricing.
intro: The all-new iPad mini features an 8.5-inch OLED screen, A20 Pro silicon, and IP67 water resistance.
html:
Apple has officially unveiled its next-generation iPad mini, bringing some of the biggest upgrades to its compact tablet lineup. Announced on October 26, 2026, the new iPad mini features a larger 8.5-inch OLED display, the powerful A20 Pro chip, a thinner and lighter design, and IP67-rated water and dust resistance.

The latest model also introduces enhanced AI capabilities with iPadOS 27, improved wireless connectivity, a landscape-oriented front camera, and a new Acoustic Display audio system. With these upgrades, Apple aims to deliver a more powerful iPad experience in a compact form factor for students, professionals, content creators, and everyday users.

What's New in iPad mini 8th Gen

  • Display: Larger 8.5-inch Super Retina XDR OLED (replaces the 8.3-inch LCD)
  • Processor: 2nm Apple A20 Pro chip (up to 60% faster CPU, 2.7x faster GPU)
  • Design & Weight: Ultra-slim 5.4mm body and 255g weight (thinner bezels, over 40g lighter)
  • Durability: Official IP67 water and dust resistance (first ever on an iPad)
  • Front Camera: 12MP Center Stage moved to the landscape edge for natural video calls
  • Audio: Sealed Acoustic Display stereo system projecting sound directly through the screen
  • Wireless: Apple N1 chip adding Wi-Fi 7, Bluetooth 6, and Thread support
  • OS: Ships with iPadOS 27 featuring Apple Intelligence and Siri AI

8.5-inch OLED Display with Brighter Visuals

The most exciting change is the screen. Apple swapped the older 8.3-inch LCD for a vibrant 8.5-inch OLED panel. Apple trimmed the borders around the screen by 24%. Because of this, the tablet itself has not grown larger in your hands. You simply get more screen space in the same compact footprint. The resolution sits at 2316 x 1512 (326 ppi), meaning text and pictures stay pin-sharp.

OLED completely transforms the viewing experience. Individual pixels light up and turn off on their own. This means you get true inky blacks, vibrant colors, and a massive 2,000,000:1 contrast ratio. The screen is also twice as bright as before. It reaches up to 1,200 nits when watching HDR videos, and 600 nits during normal daytime use. If you like reading in bed, it can dim down to a single nit to save your eyes in a dark room.

The catch here is that the screen stays locked at 60Hz. Apple did not include its ultra-smooth 120Hz ProMotion tech on this model. While movies and books look gorgeous, fast Apple Pencil sketches and rapid scrolling will not feel quite as snappy as they do on an iPad Pro.

A20 Pro Chip Brings Fast Performance

The new iPad mini is powered by Apple's A20 Pro chip, built using a 2-nanometer manufacturing process. According to Apple, the new iPad mini delivers:

  • Up to 60% faster multithreaded CPU performance.

  • Up to 2.7 times faster graphics, including hardware-accelerated ray tracing for console-grade gaming.

  • Up to 4.5 times faster AI processing for instant editing and generative features.

There is an important hardware detail to check before buying. Not every storage size has the exact same processor setup. The 128GB and 256GB models feature a 5-core CPU and a 16-core Neural Engine. The 512GB model gets the full A20 Pro chip, packing a faster 6-core CPU, double the memory bandwidth, and a 32-core Dual Neural Engine.

If you mostly read, stream, take notes, and play casual games, the 128GB or 256GB model will be plenty fast. But if you plan to edit 4K video or run heavy on-device AI apps, the 512GB model offers noticeably more efficiency.

Thinner Body and Real IP67 Water Resistance

Apple managed to shave the iPad mini down to just 5.4mm thick, down from 6.3mm on the older version. Weight has also dropped to 255 grams, so it feels remarkably light in one hand. Because the chassis is slightly narrower and visibly thinner, older rigid snap-on cases will not fit this model. You will need a new case designed specifically for this body.

Even better, it finally comes with an official IP67 rating for dust and water resistance. This is a first for any iPad model. Laboratory tests show it can survive immersion in up to 1 meter of water for 30 minutes. While you should not take it swimming intentionally, you no longer need to worry about drink spills or sudden rain showers. Keep in mind that Apple's standard warranty still excludes liquid damage.

Better Cameras for Everyday Video Calls

Apple fixed the biggest annoyance with the front camera by moving it to the long landscape edge. When you prop your tablet up horizontally for a video call or online class, you look directly at the lens instead of off to the side. Center Stage also follows your movement automatically to keep you in frame.

On the back, the 12MP camera captures clean 4K video at 60 fps. It now includes an Adaptive True Tone flash. This smart flash detects documents and removes annoying shadows when scanning receipts, notes, or paperwork in dim lighting.

Acoustic Display: Sound That Plays Through the Glass

To make the tablet waterproof without open speaker holes on the sides, Apple engineered an audio solution called the Acoustic Display. The system uses specially designed woofers to produce deeper bass and higher volume, while custom tweeters deliver clearer high-frequency sound. These components are integrated into the display and enclosure rather than relying on conventional speaker openings.

Instead of traditional speaker grills, custom woofers sit right behind the screen and project bass and midrange sound through the glass. Dedicated tweeters sit discreetly along the side seams for crisp high notes. The result is louder, richer stereo sound with punchier bass, all while keeping the tablet completely sealed against water and dust.

Wi-Fi 7, Bluetooth 6, and Fast 5G

The new iPad mini introduces Apple's N1 wireless networking chip, bringing support for Wi-Fi 7, Bluetooth 6, and Thread. Apple says the N1 chip improves performance on 5GHz Wi-Fi networks and enhances the reliability of features such as AirDrop and AirPlay.

If you pick the cellular model, Apple's new C2 modem provides up to 50% faster 5G data speeds while using less battery. It uses a digital eSIM instead of a physical plastic tray, making it effortless to add data plans when traveling. The USB-C port also supports USB 3 data transfer speeds up to 10Gbps, so offloading large files to an external drive takes only seconds.

iPadOS 27, Apple Intelligence, and Desk-Sized Multitasking

The new iPad mini runs iPadOS 27, bringing a full suite of Apple Intelligence features to the small screen. A redesigned Siri AI arrives in beta, capable of understanding on-screen context and answering complex questions using your personal context. You also get built-in photo clean-up tools to erase background clutter, alongside generative image creation. All of these features are processed privately on the device.

The biggest productivity perk arrives with iPadOS 27.2 in the form of extended display mode. When you plug the iPad mini into an external monitor using a USB-C cable, it no longer just mirrors your screen. It lets you run an independent desktop with separate, resizable windows, turning this tiny slate into a genuine little workstation at your desk.

Apple Pencil Pro and Smart Folio Support

The new iPad mini supports both Apple Pencil Pro and Apple Pencil (USB-C), giving users options for note-taking, drawing, sketching, and digital productivity.

Apple Pencil Pro is the top pick for artists and note-takers. It offers advanced features such as squeeze and barrel roll, along with Find My support to help locate the stylus if misplaced. The USB-C version is a more affordable option for basic writing and sketching.

Apple also launched a redesigned magnetic Smart Folio made of durable TechWoven fabric. Available in Navy Blue and Taupe, it snaps onto the thinner frame and offers multiple viewing angles for typing, reading, and streaming.

Apple iPad mini (A20 Pro) vs iPad mini (A17 Pro)

Feature New iPad mini (A20 Pro, 2026) Previous iPad mini (A17 Pro, 2024)

Screen Resolution 2316 x 1512 at 326 ppi 2266 x 1488 at 326 ppi
Peak brightness 1,200 nits HDR / 600 nits SDR 500 nits SDR

CPU Setup 5-core (128/256GB) / 6-core (512GB) 6-core across all models
Graphics 7-core GPU with Ray Tracing 5-core GPU

Thickness & Weight 5.4mm thin and 255 grams 6.3mm thin and 297 grams
Storage options 128GB, 256GB, 512GB 128GB, 256GB, 512GB

Final Thoughts: Should You Upgrade?

The new Apple iPad mini brings meaningful improvements to Apple's compact tablet lineup. Its larger OLED display, A20 Pro chip, slimmer design, IP67 water and dust resistance, improved cameras, and faster connectivity make it a more capable device for everyday use and demanding applications.

For most people, the 256GB model is the sweet spot. It gives you twice the space of the base model without pushing your budget. Only consider the top-tier 512GB model if you specifically need the unbinned 6-core chip and 32-core Neural Engine for heavy video editing or machine learning work.

That said, the price increase and the 60Hz screen might make some buyers think twice. If you just want a simple tablet for browsing the web, reading ebooks, or basic note-taking, an older A17 Pro iPad mini 7 will save you a lot of money. But if you want the best portable screen, weatherproofing, and desktop-class power in a device you can hold in one hand, the new iPad mini is tough to beat.
